newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain union sees room to raise public '98 spending.
newsitem.headline: Spain union sees room to raise public '98 spending.

text.p: Spain's General Workers Union UGT sees room for a more expansive 1998 budget after reductions made in this year's plan, a UGT official told Spanish radio on Thursday.

"There is scope in the 1998 budget, given that revenues are performing as expected, to raise spending in a moderate way and concentrate it on productive investment, maintaining social spending and paying public employees adequately," Toni Ferrer, head of union action at UGT told Spanish radio.

For the 1997 budget, the conservative Spanish government froze public sector workers' salaries in its drive to cut the deficit to three percent of gross domestic product -- the reference value set for participation in Europe's single currency.
It plans to continue austere spending. In a three-year plan, the deficit is seen declining to 2.5 percent in 1998.
"In 1998, we will have to recover lost buying power (for public workers) ...and we will have to negotiate how we recover part or all of that," he said.
